properties.areaDesc: Highlands
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 21 at 4:52PM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
At 452 PM EST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm
capable of producing a funnel cloud over Sebring Regional Airport,
or near Sebring, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Funnel clouds and wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible. Gusty winds
could knock down tree limbs and blow around unsecured
objects.

Locations impacted include...
Sebring, Sebring Regional Airport, Lake Istokpoga, Avon Park Air
Force Range, and Lorida.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.areaDesc: Orange
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 21 at 4:49PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
At 449 PM EST, Doppler radar was tracking a shower over Sea World, or
6 miles east of Bay Lake, moving northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph. Funnel cloud is possible.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Orlando, Windermere, Bay Lake, Oak Ridge, Conway, Orlando
International Airport, Pine Hills, Belle Isle, Universal Studios,
Sea World, Doctor Phillips, Pine Castle, Bay Hill, Hunters Creek,
Orlovista, Edgewood, Lake Buena Vista, Tangelo Park, Sky Lake and
Williamsburg.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Conditions are favorable for the development of weak, brief funnel
clouds. On rare occasions they can briefly touch down, producing wind
gusts over 50 mph. If a funnel cloud is spotted move indoors and
report your sighting to the National Weather Service.

properties.areaDesc: Aguada, PR; Moca, PR
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 5:43PM AST until November 21 at 8:45PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Aguada and Moca...

* WHEN...Until 845 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable. River or stream flows
are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 540 PM AST, heavy rainfall from earlier today will likely
cause small stream flooding. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain fell.
- Rio Culebrinas is the most likely place to experience minor
flooding. Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional
rainfall is expected.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 1:40PM PST until November 22 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to
2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and
low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation
along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above
ground level.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...From 7 AM to 3 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast
may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning.
While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of
coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides
early next week.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

properties.areaDesc: Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 21 at 4:28PM EST until November 21 at 5:30PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 530 PM EST.

* At 427 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 27 nm east of Sunny Isles, moving northwest
at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.description:

expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4
AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST
Tuesday through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase
next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be
Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides
each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2
feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records set back in
late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain
around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell
Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf
beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf
heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10
feet on west-facing beaches.

NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical
predictions based on trends in recent observations.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 4:23PM AST until November 22 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo.

* WHEN...Through 6 AM AST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.areaDesc: Broward, FL
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 2:58PM EST until November 21 at 5:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Broward County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other
areas is occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 257 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Fort Lauderdale, Pembroke Pines, Hollywood, Miramar, Davie,
Plantation, Hallandale, Dania Beach, Cooper City, West Park,
Chambers Estates, Nova Southeastern University, Oak Point, Royal
Palm Ranches, Estates Of Fort Lauderdale, Broadview Park,
Ravenswood Estates, Sunshine Acres and Pine Island Ridge.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 11:55AM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Most susceptible time of
flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides
between about 730 AM and 930 AM.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Santa Barbara
County Southwestern Coast and Santa Barbara County
Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...From 3 AM Monday to 3 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to high surf is
expected much of the week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday.
Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 3 AM MONDAY TO 3 PM PST THURSDAY

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 21 at 11:55AM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to
11 feet building to 15 to 20 feet Wednesday with dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be
around the time of the morning high tides between about 800 AM
and 1000 AM.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 3 PM
PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday
to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is likely. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. The High Surf Advisory
will likely be needed to be upgraded to a High Surf Warning
before Wednesday. Additional products will likely be needed
into Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 21 at 11:49AM PST until November 27 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, coastal flooding
possible.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4
AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday
night through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Major flooding, up to two foot above ground level,
during high tides is possible along the immediate coast as well
as low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of
the coastal rivers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal
overflow flooding is expected. Coastal residents in the warned
area should be alert for rising water, and take appropriate
action to protect life and property.

A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be
alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to
protect property.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 2:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination
with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St
Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through the middle of next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 21 at 10:24AM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at
8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM
Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday,
2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4
ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These
predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the

properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS
EVENING TO 10 AM EST SUNDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 2:45AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SUNDAY EVENING

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 313 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert on Saturday for the
Susquehanna Valley.

A Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for
sensitive groups. Sensitive groups include children, people
suffering from asthma, heart disease or other lung diseases,
and the elderly. The effects of air pollution can be minimized
by avoiding strenuous activity or exercise outdoors.

For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles,
visit www.airnow.gov, and www.aqpartners.state.pa.us.

have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November
22nd.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:
